workflows.name: Authentication & Route Protection
workflows.summary: Clerk middleware intercepts every request; any path matching /dashboard(.*) calls auth().protect(), redirecting unauthenticated visitors to /signin and unauthorised users to /dashboard/stores.

steps.text: Every incoming request passes through clerkMiddleware defined in src/middleware.ts.
createRouteMatcher(['/dashboard(.*)']) tests the request URL; only paths under /dashboard are protected — all other routes (lobby, checkout, API) are public.
For protected routes, auth().protect() is invoked with unauthenticatedUrl='/signin' and unauthorizedUrl='/dashboard/stores', enforcing Clerk session presence.
The middleware matcher covers all pages, root, and api/trpc paths, excluding static assets and _next internals.

workflows.name: Add to Cart
workflows.summary: A visitor clicks 'Add to cart' from a product card or the product detail page form. The addToCart server action validates input, checks product inventory, then creates or updates a cart row in PostgreSQL, storing items as a JSON column. The cartId is persisted in a cookie.

steps.text: Visitor clicks 'Add to cart' on a product card (default variant button) or submits the quantity form on the product detail page.

evidence.note: Add to cart button in card grid/list view
Form submit handler in detail page

steps.text: Both entry points import and call the addToCart server action with { productId, quantity }.
addToCart parses rawInput against cartItemSchema (productId string, quantity ≥ 0) before any DB work.
The action queries the products table to confirm the product exists and has sufficient inventory before touching the cart.
If no cartId cookie exists, a new cart row is inserted into the carts table with items=[input] and the returned id is stored as a cookie.
If the cookie cartId refers to a closed or expired cart, the stale row is deleted and a new cart is created.

evidence.note: delete stale cart then insert fresh one

steps.text: If an open cart exists, the items JSON array is mutated in memory (quantity incremented or new item appended) then written back with db.update(carts).set({items}).
revalidatePath('/') is called so the header cart count re-renders on the next request.
The action returns { data: cart.items, error: null } on success or { data: null, error: string } on failure — never throws.

workflows.name: Checkout & Payment
workflows.summary: Customer navigates from cart to a per-store checkout page. The server calls createPaymentIntent to calculate the order total, create a Stripe PaymentIntent (connected account), and store the clientSecret in the carts table. The browser renders Stripe Elements; on submission stripe.confirmPayment redirects to a success page where payment is verified and order records are written by the Stripe webhook.

steps.text: Customer visits /cart; CheckoutCard fetches cart items per store via getCart({ storeId }) and renders a link to /checkout/{storeId}.
The checkout page server component calls getStripeAccount({ storeId }) to verify the seller has a connected Stripe account.

evidence.note: getStripeAccount — queries stores + payments, calls stripe.accounts.retrieve

steps.text: createPaymentIntent is called server-side; it calculates the order total (src/lib/checkout.ts), calls stripe.paymentIntents.create on the seller's connected account, then stores paymentIntentId and clientSecret in the carts table.

evidence.note: createPaymentIntent call, result passed as promise

steps.text: CheckoutShell initialises the Stripe Elements provider with the clientSecret; CheckoutForm renders LinkAuthenticationElement, AddressElement, and PaymentElement.
On form submit, stripe.confirmPayment is called in the browser with a return_url of /checkout/{storeId}/success.
The success page calls getPaymentIntent to retrieve and verify the Stripe PaymentIntent status is 'succeeded' and the cartId matches.
Stripe asynchronously POSTs a payment_intent.succeeded webhook to /api/webhooks/stripe; the handler inserts into addresses and orders, decrements product inventory, and marks the cart closed=true.

evidence.note: payment_intent.succeeded: addresses INSERT, orders INSERT, products UPDATE, carts UPDATE closed=true

steps.text: If the webhook has not fired by the time the success page loads, getOrderLineItems contains a fallback that manually creates address, order, updates inventory, and closes the cart.

workflows.name: Seller Product Management
workflows.summary: An authenticated seller creates a store via onboarding, optionally connects Stripe, then adds, updates, or deletes products through dashboard pages. Product images are uploaded to Uploadthing before the server action inserts/updates the products table. All mutations revalidate the relevant Next.js cache paths.

steps.text: Seller visits /onboarding; Clerk auth() checks userId, redirecting to /signin if absent. The Onboarding component shows the Intro step first.

evidence.note: step state machine: intro → create → connect

steps.text: Seller submits the CreateStore form; createStore server action inserts into the stores table (name, description, userId, slug) and revalidates stores cache tag.

evidence.note: CreateStore form + createStore() call on submit

steps.text: After store creation, the seller is prompted to connect Stripe via ConnectStripe; they may skip to navigate directly to /store/{storeId}.
Seller navigates to /dashboard/store/{storeId}/products/new; the page server-fetches categories and subcategories, then renders CreateProductForm.
Seller fills the product form and picks image files; clicking 'Add Product' first uploads files to Uploadthing via the productImage endpoint (max 4 MB, max 3 files, Clerk-authenticated).

After upload resolves, addProduct server action is called; it checks for duplicate product names, then inserts a new row into the products table (including images as JSON) and revalidates the products path.
Seller visits /dashboard/store/{storeId}/products/{productId}; the page fetches the product row and renders UpdateProductForm pre-populated with existing data including stored images.
Seller submits the update form; same upload-then-action sequence runs: uploadFiles → updateProduct server action verifies ownership then runs db.update(products) and revalidates the product path.
Seller clicks 'Delete Product'; deleteProduct server action verifies ownership then runs db.delete(products) and revalidates the products list path.

workflows.name: Data Layer (DB Client & Schema)
workflows.summary: A single Drizzle ORM client is constructed in src/db/index.ts using the postgres driver and DATABASE_URL from validated env. All table definitions are declared in src/db/schema/ and re-exported through the index barrel. The client is imported project-wide as 'db' to run queries and mutations.

steps.text: DATABASE_URL is validated at startup by @t3-oss/env-nextjs in src/env.js; missing or malformed values throw before the server boots.

evidence.note: env validation schema — DATABASE_URL is a required server var

steps.text: src/db/index.ts creates a postgres driver client from env.DATABASE_URL, then passes it to drizzle() with the full schema object, exporting the db singleton.
src/db/schema/index.ts barrel-exports all 13 table modules: addresses, carts, categories, customers, notifications, orders, payments, products, stocks, stores, subcategories, tags, variants.

evidence.note: 14 export * lines covering all schema modules

steps.text: Every schema file spreads lifecycleDates (createdAt/updatedAt) into its table and exports Foo/$inferSelect and NewFoo/$inferInsert types.

evidence.note: lifecycleDates helper — inferred from AGENTS.md convention

steps.text: Drizzle config in drizzle.config.ts points the dialect to postgresql, the schema entry to src/db/schema/index.ts, and migrations output to ./drizzle/.
All db:* npm scripts are prefixed with dotenv-cli so DATABASE_URL from .env is injected before drizzle-kit runs; direct drizzle-kit invocations without dotenv will fail.

evidence.note: dotenv prefix on db:generate, db:push, db:migrate, db:seed scripts
